name: Sunbelt Vantage
_identity: THE RENTAL. Light, cheap, and eager in a way that never pays off: the quickest rack in the fleet (steer_speed 9.2, 36 deg lock) bolted to the worst tires (0.98) and the weakest engine (9800 N) and a nose full of weight (com_forward 0.30). Turn in hard and the front just leaves -- it understeers into a slide, always, and the soft pedal (24500) means you arrive at the corner too fast to argue about it. The rear handbrake locking two undriven wheels is the only rotation available. Everything about it is rented.
_tuning_math: corner mass = 1380/4 = 345 kg; static load = 345*9.81 = 3384.5 N; spring_rate 39000 N/m -> static compression = 3384.5/39000 = 0.0868 m = 25.5% of suspension_rest 0.34 (dead centre of the 20-30% target: this car has no opinions); critical damping = 2*sqrt(39000*345) = 7336 N*s/m; damping 2950 = 0.402 * critical -- one soft bounce, a little dive, nothing dangerous. Ground sits 0.873 m below the body origin at static ride, so com_height -0.35 puts the CoM 0.523 m up. Static rollover threshold = half-track / CoM height = 0.81/0.523 = ~1.55 g against tire_friction 0.98 -- it slides at 0.98 g and NEVER rolls, which is the entire personality. Front-drive traction limit: front axle carries (1.48+0.30)/2.90 = 61.4% of 1380 kg = 8311 N, x0.98 = 8145 N of grip against only 9800 N of engine, so it is ENGINE-limited almost everywhere and measures 5.17 s to 20 m/s -- slower than the cruiser, slower than the truck, faster only than the Slab. The first draft ran 14200 N and clocked 3.17 s, i.e. the rental out-dragged the Interceptor, which is a joke the fiction cannot afford.
_track_change_cycle2: TRACK 1.62 -> 1.70 (D-021). Same story as the Slab, smaller: the 1.9 m shell stood 20.0 mm outboard of its own tyre, which both failed the tyre-vs-lip row and hid the tread behind the flank. Widening the track to 1.70 puts the tyre face at 0.970 so the builder's BEAM_INSET clamp costs only 2 mm of beam instead of 42 mm per side. HANDLING CONSEQUENCE: +4.9% track = +10.1% roll stiffness, load transfer -4.7%, rollover margin improves. track_width is a SINGLE value here, so front and rear roll stiffness move together and the roll-stiffness DISTRIBUTION is unchanged -- the understeer balance that is this car's ratified D-012 identity (quick rack, weak engine, pushes wide) is a function of that distribution and of steer_falloff, and neither moves. Engine, brakes, mass, steering and suspension rates are untouched.
